clue.text: Short skirts in modern surroundings are suggestive

indicators.note: the skirts go in, placed within the next word's letters
the modern word forms the surroundings, wrapping round the skirts

explanation.surface: A remark that miniskirts in a contemporary setting send a suggestive message.
explanation.walkthrough: Two indicators share the work: 'in' and 'surroundings' both say one piece is wrapped by the other. 'are suggestive' must be read as 'are reminiscent (of)' for the swap to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reminiscent calls another thing to mind, which is to say it is evocative of it.

clue.text: Once more, act fast and suggestive

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A director asks for another take, done quickly and with innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means evocative or reminiscent of something.

clue.text: Dustin's original character in "Rainman" mangled the language

indicators.note: mangled shows the letters are crushed into a new order
the original of a name is its first letter, so take the opening of Dustin's

explanation.surface: Dustin Hoffman's character in the film Rain Man is said to mangle his speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character in' is link padding for the film picture: D (from 'Dustin's original') joins RAINMAN and 'mangled' rearranges all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the main spoken form of Chinese, a tongue spoken by hundreds of millions.

clue.text: Leaders of nations agree on message implicating Campbell, for instance

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters, read in order

explanation.surface: Heads of state agree on a statement that implicates someone called Campbell.
explanation.walkthrough: Naomi Campbell is a British supermodel, so 'Campbell, for instance' defines the first name by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Supermodel Naomi Campbell is an example of a person with this first name.

clue.text: People redrafted his law on independence

indicators.note: a redrafted text is rewritten, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the standard abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A nation rewrites his law on independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redrafted' rearranges the first two words of fodder; the independence letter is spelt after them, and 'on' is a link. 'People' looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swahili are an East African ethnic group, also giving their name to a widely spoken tongue.

clue.text: Idiot got up, looked outside and tried…

indicators.note: the looked word goes outside, wrapping the idiot
in a down clue, got up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A fool stood up, glanced about and had a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' reverses the idiot because this is a down clue, read upward; 'outside' wraps the looked word round it. The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it, an old-fashioned word for having a go.

clue.text: … to beat a former Spice Girl (Geordie) with fruit

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls
a Geordie comes from Tyneside, in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: An ellipsis continues: to thrash an ex-pop star from Newcastle with a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne, in England's North East, giving NE. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small loose-skinned citrus, a variety of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Whippet?

parts.note: split as whip plus pet: one word that is both a lash and a household animal

explanation.walkthrough: A whippet is a racing dog, which leads away from the split: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip and a domestic feline is a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails was a naval whip, and a domestic feline is a common pet.

clue.text: Stop taking runs, and stay here

indicators.note: the stop word takes in, or contains, the runs

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer is told to stop running between wickets and remain at home base.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the marked line where a batsman is safe; a batsman who stops taking runs stays in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The batting crease is the marked area a batsman stays inside to avoid being run out.

clue.text: This tea sounds healthy

parts.note: the herbal drink's name is pronounced like 'tis sane, an old way of saying that it is of sound mind

explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, the name of this herbal infusion is a contraction of 'it is' followed by a word for mentally sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is an herbal infusion drunk as a tea.

clue.text: Wild animal's doing nothing right

indicators.note: the nothing letter shifts to the right within the word

explanation.surface: A wild creature is doing nothing at all, quite correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' moves the O in DOING further right, after the N. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is Australia's feral wild dog.

clue.text: Beat sense into those who fail to turn up

definitions.text: those who fail to turn up

indicators.note: read as 'made into', a change of form that rearranges the letters

explanation.surface: A teacher would knock some sense into pupils who skip class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like the anagram signal, but the letters of BEAT and SENSE are both fodder, with 'into' signalling their rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Absentees are people missing from where they are expected to be.

clue.text: Responsibility half lies with the skill

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word means its first two letters

explanation.surface: Blame lies partly with the one who has the know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the' links LI, the first half of 'lies', to ABILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A liability is a legal obligation, something one is answerable for.

clue.text: Countess entranced, discovering German town

indicators.note: dis-covering, taking the cover off, exposes letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A countess, spellbound, finds a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovering' signals letters exposed inside 'countESS ENtranced'.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in Germany's Ruhr valley.

clue.text: Town in Africa backing Scotsman to steal one

indicators.note: backing means read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a stereotypical Scottish man's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Scot supports a plan to steal something in an African town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IAN into NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Ancient type of bridge could be condemned here

parts.note: a Bailey bridge is a prefabricated military bridge

explanation.surface: An old bridge design might be pronounced unsafe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bailey is London's Central Criminal Court, where convicts are sentenced, so a person could be condemned there.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Central Criminal Court passes sentence on those found guilty.

clue.text: Swim across the river and get wet

indicators.note: the swim spans across the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a dip is a short swim

explanation.surface: Swim over the river and end up soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts DIP round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To drip is to be so soaked that water falls in drops.

clue.text: Bloke got up to ring short bondsman for national

indicators.note: in a down clue, got up means read from bottom to top
short means cut, here losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A man stood up to telephone a servant on behalf of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' turns GUY into YUG; 'short' docks SLAVE to SLAV. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, here the former Balkan federation.

clue.text: Clock for commercial traveller and consumer

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: A timepiece meant for a salesman and a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: A repeater is a clock or watch that strikes the last hour again when a button is pressed. 'for' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater watch chimes the time again on demand.

clue.text: Hero's declared to be resting

indicators.note: said out loud, so the next word is heard, not spelt

explanation.surface: A champion is announced as taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a much-admired figure, someone revered.

clue.text: Support draw? It's a joke!

explanation.surface: Someone asks for help drawing, then admits they were kidding.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-pull is a teasing hoax played on someone.

clue.text: Disheartened performer to miss the introduction

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outside letters of performer remain

parts.note: to elude is to escape or miss

explanation.surface: A dispirited actor skips the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelude is an opening piece, preceding the main work.

clue.text: Not a medicine to put on brow, oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first and third

explanation.surface: A dose that is not real medicine is applied to the forehead in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links PLACE to BO, the first and third letters of 'brow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active drug.

clue.text: Gamble over a ship's dog

indicators.note: the gamble goes over, covering the a and ship

explanation.surface: Someone bets on the hound aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' can mean placed around; SS is the usual prefix for a steamship, as in SS Great Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound with long ears.

clue.text: Firm over discount voucher

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a firm
upon means on top of, over

explanation.surface: A company supplies money-off vouchers.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon gives money off a purchase.

clue.text: A computer memory has a particular smell

explanation.surface: A computer's memory has a distinctive odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive scent.

clue.text: Politician with whom lads get on, in other words

indicators.note: the letters say the same thing in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A statesman popular with young men.
explanation.walkthrough: W.E. Gladstone was a Victorian British Prime Minister. 'with whom' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone was a four-time Liberal Prime Minister of Britain.

clue.text: Employees getting stick

explanation.surface: Staff are given a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: The workers of an organisation, and also a walking pole.

clue.text: Place for burial plot upset rule

indicators.note: to plot is to arrange, so the letters are redistributed

explanation.surface: A dispute over a grave rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are fodder; 'plot' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepulture is the act or place of interment, as in a tomb.

clue.text: Assign a charge for reversing

indicators.note: a toll is charged for turning, so the charge is read back to front

explanation.surface: A fee for turning a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for reversing' turns TOLL into LLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to allocate or distribute.

clue.text: Can it be held back?

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in reverse
the letters are held within the two words

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether something can be restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, 'caN IT' gives the answer, and the answer is a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin is a metal can for food.

clue.text: Disease that makes one scream with pain, loudly and continually?

parts.note: ow is a cry of pain

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word is heard not spelt

explanation.surface: An illness that leaves a person yelling in pain non-stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' means FOREVER said fast sounds like FEVER. 'that makes one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow fever is a viral tropical infection spread by mosquitoes.
